## Summary

**MOVE sr** (Move from status register ( & Set/clear bit 11 )).

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `sr → d` |
| Syntax | `MOVE sr,<ea>` |
| Description | Moves status register to the destination. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–6 | `0100000011` |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |

- Size is word

### Notes

- PRIVILEGED INSTRUCTION.
- Except on the 68000 & 68080 where reading the status register may be done in user mode.
- Also apollo-bit 11 is the only one that can be set/cleared in user mode.
- Ori #$800,sr & andi #$f7ff,sr will not cause a privilege exception on the 080.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have MOVE from SR. This page covers only the 68080 addition: reading SR in user mode, and setting or clearing SR bit 11 in user mode. For the classic forms, the Motorola manual applies.
- On the 68010–68060, MOVE from SR is privileged. On the 68000 and the 68080, user mode may read SR.

## Do / Don't

- DO use `ori #$800,sr` / `andi #$f7ff,sr` to set or clear the Apollo bit in user mode; other SR bits stay privileged.
